title: Science and Religion
subtitle: Why scientific discovery and belief in Allah are not competing explanations
summary: Science investigates patterns and causes within the natural world. Islam asks why an ordered world exists, why human reason can understand it, and how knowledge should be used. Scientific success does not establish atheism, while faith in Allah does not remove the need for evidence. The Quran invites observation and directs discovery toward humility, worship, and moral responsibility.

sections.title: Science Explains Creation; It Does Not Replace the Creator
sections.body: Science studies patterns and causes in nature. Islam also asks why an ordered world exists, why reason can understand it, and how knowledge should be used. Science does not establish atheism. Islam does not remove the need for evidence.

sections.title: What Science Can—and Cannot—Answer
sections.body: Science uses observation, measurement, experiment, models, and criticism. It can explain stars, disease, and inherited traits. It does not measure why anything exists, whether duties are real, or whether life has ultimate purpose. Those are philosophical and religious questions.

sections.title: The Quran Invites People to Observe
sections.body:
The Quran treats the natural world as evidence that should awaken thought:

إِنَّ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ

“Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.” (Quran 3:190)

It also says:

قُلْ سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ بَدَأَ ٱلْخَلْقَ ۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ

“Say, [O Muhammad], "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed Allah, over all things, is competent."” (Quran 29:20)

These verses are not equations or experiments. They give inquiry a spiritual setting: creation is intelligible, observation matters, and knowledge should lead to humility before Allah.

sections.title: Scientific Method Is Not Atheism
sections.body: Science often seeks testable natural mechanisms. Muslims can use that method fully. Studying rainfall does not deny that Allah sustains it. Metaphysical naturalism claims that nature is all that exists. No experiment can establish that universal claim.

sections.title: Why Islam Gives Science a Home
sections.body: Science assumes stable patterns and minds able to discover them. Islam grounds both in one wise Creator. It also teaches that ability is not moral permission and knowledge is a trust. This explains an ordered world without placing God inside a scientific gap.

sections.title: Evolution and Human Origins
sections.body: Evolutionary biology has evidence from genetics, fossils, geography, and observed change. Muslims should not misrepresent it. Views differ about how the evidence relates to Adam. The Quran's theological claims and science should each be stated precisely. Honest disagreement is better than false consensus.

sections.title: Use Scientific-Sign Arguments Carefully
sections.body: Claims that a verse secretly contains a modern discovery can depend on one translation or changing science. Ask what the Arabic means, how early readers understood it, and whether the match is specific. Compatibility may be meaningful, but it is not automatic proof.

sections.title: Knowledge as a Path to God
sections.body: Islam welcomes truthful investigation because nature and revelation come from the same God. Science describes creation. Tawhid explains why creation is ordered, dependent, meaningful, and entrusted to people. The Quran invites observation and points to the one Creator.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body: **Does science disprove God?** No. Science studies testable mechanisms. The claim that nothing exists beyond them is philosophy, not a lab result. **Is the Quran a science textbook?** No. It calls nature signs and encourages observation. **Must Muslims reject evolution?** Muslim views differ, especially about Adam; the evidence and the theology should both be stated honestly.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:
- **Islam's Quantum Question** — Nidhal Guessoum. A critical Muslim engagement with science and Islamic thought.
- **Science and Religion: A Very Short Introduction** — Thomas Dixon. A short history of the debate.
- **Where the Conflict Really Lies** — Alvin Plantinga. A philosophical study of science and naturalism.

faq.question: Does science disprove God?
faq.answer: No. Science studies testable natural mechanisms. The claim that nothing exists beyond those mechanisms is a philosophical form of naturalism, not a laboratory result.

faq.question: Is the Quran a science textbook?
faq.answer: No. It calls natural phenomena signs of the Creator and encourages observation, but scientific measurements and models must be established through scientific work.

faq.question: Must Muslims reject evolution?
faq.answer: Muslims hold several views, especially concerning Adam and human ancestry. Scientific evidence should be described accurately, and theological interpretations should be labeled rather than presented as unanimous.

faq.question: Can Muslims accept methodological naturalism?
faq.answer: Yes, when it means seeking testable natural causes in scientific research. It does not require the separate metaphysical belief that nature is all that exists.
